questions.question:
Six points are marked on a sheet of squared paper as shown. Which of the following shapes cannot be made by connecting some of these points using straight lines?
Choices:
A:parallelogram
B:trapezium
C:right-angled triangle
D:obtuse-angled triangle
E:all the shapes $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{D}$ can be made

In triangle $P Q R$, a point $S$ is chosen on the line segment $Q R$, then a point $T$ is chosen on the line segment $P S$. Considering the nine marked angles, what is the smallest number of different values that these nine angles could take?

A rectangular piece of paper $6$ inches wide is folded as in the diagram so that one corner touches the opposite side. The length in inches of the crease $L$ in terms of angle $\theta$ is
Choices:
A:$3\sec ^2\theta\csc\theta$
B:$6\sin\theta\sec\theta$
C:$3\sec\theta\csc\theta$
D:$6\sec\theta\csc ^2\theta$
E:$\text{None of these}$
The structure shown is glued together from 10 cubes. Its entire exterior, including the bottom, is painted. How many cube faces are painted?
A wall around a square area is made from 36 identical cubes. A section of the wall is shown. How many cubes are needed to completely fill the square area?

The cube shown is built from equally sized bricks. The shortest side of one brick is $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ long. What are the dimensions of one brick in $\mathrm{cm}$?
Choices:
A:$4 \times 6 \times 12$
B:$4 \times 6 \times 16$
C:$4 \times 8 \times 12$
D:$4 \times 8 \times 16$
E:$4 \times 12 \times 16$

It takes 9 litres of paint to cover the surface of the cube on the left.
How much paint would it take to cover the surface of the shape on the right?
Choices:
A:9 litres
B:8 litres
C:6 litres
D:4 litres
E:2 litres
The diagram shows two ordinary dice. What is the total number of spots on all the faces that cannot be seen in the diagram?
